relation: four separate representations of the edges of a cyclic vertex sequence, all by conversion: X9 x9_cycle_edges, X24 x24_cycle_edge_seq and X25 x25_cycle_edge_seq are GTBase.walks_paths.seq_cycle_edge_list c (ordered list of the pairs of zip c (rot 1 c), closing pair included); X216 x216_cycle_edges is seq_cycle_edge_set c (its finite support); Cycle XE1 xe1_cycle_edges is seq_cycle_graph_edge_set c (the actual edges among those pairs, equal to seq_cycle_edge_set c :&: E(G) for every c); U2 cycle_edges, X211 x211_cycle_edges and U9 cycle_edgesG are seq_next_edge_set c (the first-occurrence successor image, contained in the support and equal to it under uniq c)
summary: Batch B, family B11 (edges of a cyclic sequence): the eight helpers that extract the edges of a cyclic vertex sequence through `zip c (rot 1 c)` or MathComp's `next`, kept as FOUR representations, each convertible to its `GTBase.walks_paths` canonical. The raw ordered list `map (fun p => [set p.1; p.2]) (zip c (rot 1 c))` (Cycle X9 `x9_cycle_edges`, Cycle X24 `x24_cycle_edge_seq`, Packing X25 `x25_cycle_edge_seq`) is `seq_cycle_edge_list c`; its raw finite support (GTMisc X216 `x216_cycle_edges`) is `seq_cycle_edge_set c`; Cycle XE1's actual-edge filter `xe1_cycle_edges` (adjacent endpoints whose pair occurs in either order) is `seq_cycle_graph_edge_set c`; the first-occurrence successor image `[set [set x; next c x] | x in [set z | z \in c]]` (Hamilton U2 `cycle_edges`, Hamilton X211 `x211_cycle_edges` and the cross-name Packing U9 `cycle_edgesG`) is `seq_next_edge_set c`. Signatures and the explicit `Arguments` of U2, X211 and U9 are unchanged, and no adjacency, uniqueness or length guard is added to any helper. API: the succession bridges `seq_next_in_zip` (every sequence) and `seq_zip_nextE` (under `uniq c`); list size, closing pair, rotation and reversal (up to `perm_eq`); support membership through `seq_cyclic_consecutive`, closing pair, open support and rotation/reversal invariance; the filter equals support :&: E(G) for every sequence and the support under the sufficient guard `cycle (--) c`; the image is contained in the support for every sequence and equal to it under the sufficient guard `uniq c`, so all four agree on a `ucycle`; degenerate cases; groundings (one-entry loop, digon, a non-edge of K_1,2, the closing pair, and the closed walk [0; 1; 0; 2; 3] of K_4, on which the image misses {0, 2} and changes under rotation and reversal).

Eleven rows and ten intermediates, frozen with this family's helpers only: Cycle X9 (proper edge-coloured short cycle; incident-edge colouring chain), Cycle X24 (long rainbow cycle; rainbow cycle chain), Cycle XE1 #184 (cycle-or-edge pieces), Cycle XE2 #641 (cross-file edge-disjoint cycles), Packing X25 (Kotzig; Hamiltonian edge-set and perfect one-factorization chains), Packing U9 (matchings extend to Hamilton cycles of hypercubes), GTMisc X216 (second Hamilton cycle, BLOCKED; output specification), Hamilton U2 (4-connected graphs are not uniquely Hamiltonian; r-regular graphs are not uniquely Hamiltonian, with the uniquely-Hamiltonian chain; prism decomposition, with the two-cycle decomposition chain) and Hamilton X211 (Cantoni; Hamilton-cycle edge sets). Every guard, quantifier, constant, status and documented defect is unchanged, including X216's blocked complexity defect and the Hamilton digon convention and empty-carrier behaviour. The proof consumers (Hamilton grounding_U2, grounding_X211 and implications_U2, GTMisc grounding_X216) compile unchanged.

History (complete rows; every earlier frozen body, array, type, status and document unchanged): Packing X25 reuses M1's complete snapshot `Packing.migration.simple_edges.X25Legacy` (raw list, Hamiltonian edge-set chain, pre-M1 edge set, pre-C2 perfect matching; kept by C2) as this family's frozen copy, with the certificates restated in Packing.migration.cycle_edges. `X24Original` composes C2's frozen one-factorization chain with this family's frozen rainbow cycle (C2+B11), certified through C2's certificate. `X9Original`, `XE1Original` (#184) and `XE2Original` (#641, cross-file) compose B10's frozen cycle helpers with this family's frozen chains (B10+B11), by conversion. The B10 per-row X9, #184 and #641 snapshots and C2's X24 row still call live chains of this family and are documented reciprocally. M1's edge-set aliases `x9_edge_set` and `xe1_edge_set` stay live in the X9 and #184 rows and Originals: M1 froze only its helpers there.

Kernel evidence, independent of this textual report: `Print All Dependencies` of every frozen row, chain and Original contains no live helper or chain of this family and none of the four canonicals; the Originals also reach no live B10 or C2 helper or canonical; every per-row copy reaches no live constant outside its live row's closure (so U2's own `hamiltonian_cycle` / `edge_set` and X211's GTBase.common `hamiltonian_cycle` resolve as in the sources); each live row reaches its canonical and its alias (/srv/graph-theory-rocq/coordination/evidence/B11-cycle_edges/print_all_dependencies_summary.txt).

Baseline 0a0203e is the announced B10 prose pin (B10 e1dc8dd plus its wording follow-up), not yet integrated; B11 is stacked on it as assigned. No statement text, doc block, manifest row or leg state changes (checked below). The B4, B8 and B10 specs, which listed some of these helpers as untouched distinct variants, now record that B11 migrated them.

B29 (2026-10-04): the former distinct variant `Extremal.conjectures.X84.x84_cycle_edge_set` ("a predicate on an edge set (connectivity, degree and cardinality constraints), not an extractor; untouched") keeps that representation distinction from this family's sequence-to-edge extraction and was untouched by B11; since B29 it is a transparent alias of `Extremal.foundations.edge_cycles.edge_family_cycle`, owned by family cycle-lengths (class edge-family-cycles). This report checks every listed distinct variant against the B11 baseline text, which the alias changes, so the qualified note is kept here, as B11 recorded its own migrations in the B4, B8 and B10 specs.
